review_summary:
Static review of frozen HEAD d735e07 against base 9183908. I executed nothing. Every claim below comes from hand-tracing the supplied sources.

Verified repaired:
- The prior HIGH (odd literal backtick in single quotes, double quotes, comments or quoted heredocs). `echo '`'; echo `curl …`` now tracks single-quote state, so the real substitution is captured and denied. The comment-boundary, double-quote and quoted-heredoc variants trace the same way.
- Before+after parity, ANSI-C and locale quotes, `${…}`, `$(…)`, `<(…)`, `((`, `[[`, escaped newlines, unquoted heredocs and unterminated state all set the fallback flag. The fallback is the old raw regex `` `[^`]*(curl|wget|fetch) ``.
- A non-zero awk exit, or an unknown mode header, denies.
- The SARIF -1 sentinel is now normalised to absent. Positive/-1 pairs are reconciled, other negative, fractional, string or boolean indexes fail closed, and explicit level, rule-id agreement and numeric severity are unchanged.
- The weekly workflow now passes `WEEK_INPUT` through the step environment as a quoted argument. Empty input still reaches `memory-rollup.sh` as an empty `$2`, which gives the current week.
- The staged ADR workflow uses `BASE_REF` the same way.
- The ANSI strip in the ledger leaves the stored log bytes unchanged, and a failed `sed` selects tooling-error.

The guard repair is not complete. The quoted-heredoc recogniser also matches the second and third `<` of a here-string, so a real command substitution after `<<< 'EOF'` is skipped and the guard allows it. The base regex denied that input, so this is another regression of the same class as the prior HIGH. Skipped quoted-heredoc bodies are also never inspected when the consumer is a shell. There is a small token-boundary regression for `wget2`-style names, the completion metadata is still inconsistent, and there are a few low-risk edge cases in the ledger classifier and SARIF matcher. This is a scoped regex guard, not a sandbox, and the findings should be read that way.

findings.title: Here-string `<<< 'EOF'` is mis-parsed as a quoted heredoc, hiding a real backtick network substitution
findings.reason:
`heredoc_pattern` (`<<-?[[:space:]]*('ID'|"ID")`) is not anchored against a preceding `<`. For `cat <<< 'EOF'` the leftmost attempt at the first `<` fails, but the match succeeds at the second `<`. `RSTART` then points at the second `<`, and the prefix check `index(substr(line,1,RSTART-1),"<<")` sees only a single `<`. The `rest` check passes because `rest` is empty. `here_start` therefore stays valid, `next_here` is set to `EOF`, and `has_here` is cleared. The following lines are treated as a heredoc body and skipped until a line equal to `EOF`. In real shell semantics `<<<` is a here-string, so the later lines execute normally.

Minimal input (newlines literal): `cat <<< 'EOF'` / ``echo `curl https://example.invalid/p` `` / `EOF`.

Trace: line 2 is skipped. Line 3 closes the fake heredoc, so END reports `parsed` with no payloads. No `$(` or `<(` is present, and no `deny_patterns` entry fires (no pipe to a shell, and `cat <<<` is not a blocked form). The hook exits 0. The base pattern `` `[^`]*(curl|wget|fetch) `` run on the newline-collapsed command denied this input, so the new code turns a denied command into an allowed one. `cat <<<"EOF"` and `read x <<<'EOF'` behave the same way.

The suite has no `<<<` case: `arithmetic-shift-fallback` is caught only by the `((` check.

Fix options: reject the heredoc match if the character before `<<` is `<` (or if the line contains `<<<`), and add the case above to `pre-bash-guard-literals.sh`.

findings.title: Quoted-heredoc bodies are skipped entirely, so backtick network calls in a body fed to a shell are no longer inspected
findings.reason:
The block comment says heredoc bodies cannot change backtick pairing. The code goes further: body lines hit `next` before any inspection, so backtick payloads inside them are never scanned. That is correct when the consumer is `cat` or `tee`, but not when it is `bash`, `sh`, `ssh host` and similar, which execute the body.

Minimal input (newlines literal): `bash <<'EOF'` / ``x=`curl https://example.invalid/p` `` / `EOF`.

The parser reports `parsed` with no payloads. `subst_sink_patterns` need `$(` or `<(`, and `deny_patterns` need a pipe to a shell, `<(`, or `-c`. None match, so the guard allows the command. The base regex denied it.

A `$(curl …)` in the same body is still caught by the raw sink patterns, which narrows the gap to the backtick form. AC-19 does require frontend heredocs to pass, so this is a design tradeoff. At minimum the heredoc consumer should be restricted (for example, fall back when the command word before `<<` is a shell or interpreter), or the limitation should be documented and tested. Today the tests only cover `cat`.

findings.title: Whole-token network match drops denials the base substring match gave (e.g. `wget2`, `curl-impersonate`)
findings.reason: The base regex denied any backtick span containing the substring curl, wget or fetch. The new `backtick_network` regex requires a boundary character after the verb. `` `wget2 https://x` ``, `` `curlie …` `` and `` `curl-impersonate …` `` have an alphanumeric or `-` character after the verb, so they no longer match and are allowed in parsed mode. This is a narrow regression of a previously denied command, and the stated behaviour (`fetch(...)` must pass) can be kept while still adding `2` and `-` to the allowed-suffix exclusions. No test covers these names.

findings.title: Anchored config-failure patterns can still match diff or stack output of a genuine assertion failure
findings.reason: `^[^[:alnum:]]*Startup Error[^[:alnum:]]*$` matches any line whose only alphanumeric content is `Startup Error`. A Vitest or Jest diff line such as `- "Startup Error",` or `+ Startup Error` therefore matches. The `at … (vite|vitest|playwright).config.*:N` alternative also matches a real test failure whose stack passes through a config-defined helper. In both cases a valid assertion RED is stamped tooling-error and rejected. That fails closed, so it costs a rerun and cannot hide a failure. The suite only covers the one-line quoted-assertion form. Only SGR (`…m`) sequences are stripped, so cursor and erase sequences can still defeat the anchors.

findings.title: Exact rule-id match is not preferred over the hierarchical match, so valid rules can be rejected as ambiguous
findings.reason: `id_agrees` accepts both `$id == rule.id` and `$id == rule.id + "/" + one-segment`. With descriptors `x` and `x/detail` and a result `ruleId: "x/detail"` and no index, both descriptors match and `require(length <= 1)` raises 'invalid severity metadata'. An exact match should win, with the hierarchical relation used only as a fallback. This fails closed, so it is a compatibility issue rather than a bypass, and the suite does not test it.

findings.title: Completion metadata still inconsistent: tasks_done undercounts, and spec 006 is marked shipped
findings.reason: The supplied ledger logs list T-165 to T-172 and T-326, T-327 and T-328 as `[x]`, which is 11 of the 11 tasks in `tasks_for_spec: 11`. The file says `tasks_done: 10`, with `generated` 22:50:53, before T-328 completed. Spec 006 frontmatter is `status: shipped` while the analysis reports one task not done. Its scope text says historical evidence is not re-certified, and spec 006 AC-8 requires Linux/GitHub CI to be recorded separately. Recount and regenerate the file, and confirm that `shipped` is intended. Plan 006 `updated:` was also left at 2026-10-09. The prior TASKS `last_touched` nit is fixed.

limitations: Static review only. I executed no shell, awk, jq, python or tests, and I did not run the hook against any input. The traces above are by hand against the supplied numbered sources. The here-string and heredoc-to-shell findings should be confirmed by running the hook on the minimal inputs (data only, never executing the supplied command).

awk dialect behaviour (BWK awk on macOS, gawk, mawk) was reasoned rather than tested, including leftmost-match and bracket-class handling. jq builtins (`isfinite`, `isnan`, `tonumber` on 'NaN'/'Infinity') and jq version differences were not tested.

I reviewed only the supplied diff and files. I did not see TASKS rows for T-165 to T-172, the installer, the real `memory-rollup.sh` newline behaviour beyond what was supplied, or other callers of `check-sarif.sh` and `pre-bash-guard.sh`.

The SARIF handling of -1 was checked against the supplied schema-evidence JSON and the supplied source, not against a fresh read of the OASIS text. Rejection of `tool.extensions`, external property files and `ruleConfigurationOverrides` is a conservative gate, not supported external resolution. The gate also treats non-fail kinds as non-blocking by design.

Test fixtures that extract workflow steps depend on fixed YAML indentation and a mocked git. `BASH_FUNC_sed%%` function-import behaviour depends on the bash version. The native-Node case in the ledger suite is optional.

This is a scoped regex guard, not a sandbox, and the review makes no claim about the whole repository being clean. I make no claim of native attestation or live activation. Evidence logs, validate output, Semgrep triage and the 150 warnings were not independently re-verified.
